identity.title: ALMA-IMF. VII. First release of the full spectral line cubes: Core kinematics traced by DCN J = (3‒2)

This DR1 data release provides the position-position-velocity image cubes of the 12 spectral windows (spws), $\sim$6.7 GHz of bandwidth coverage per protocluster, resulting in 180 image cubes for the whole ALMA-IMF sample.

question.value: How to homogeneously calibrate and image the 12m-array spectral line cubes for the 15 ALMA-IMF protoclusters, and what are the global and core-scale kinematics traced by DCN (3-2) across different evolutionary stages?

evidence.quote: We present the data reduction steps and imaging strategies implemented to obtain the ALMA-IMF spectral line cubes.

As DCN (3-2) is expected to be an optically thin, dense gas tracer, we further utilised the DCN emission to explore the core kinematics of the $\sim$600 thermal dust cores identified and described in (cite: louvet22).

method.value: Calculate MAD (scaled by 1.4826) on the 25% of channels with the lowest intensity within manually defined continuum noise regions on JvM-corrected, non-continuum-subtracted, non-primary-beam-corrected cubes, then scale by 1/epsilon to convert to mJy per dirty beam

evidence.quote: To estimate noise levels, we use the median-absolute-deviation (MAD) estimator and take a threshold cut in intensity so that the noise is estimated using only the 25% of the channels with the lowest intensity across the full spectral window, and using the manually defined regions which were created for the continuum estimates of the noise in (cite: Ginsburg2022).

The most conservative approach to obtaining the noise, which we adopt here, is to estimate the noise from emission and line-free regions in the JvM cubes (in units of Jy per clean beam) and scale by 1/$\epsilon$ factor (see 3.5), thus, taking the higher noise estimates in units of Jy per dirty beam.

Implemented in `astropy.stats.median_abs_deviation` and we scale this by 1.4826 such that the reported value is equivalent to the standard deviation if the underlying data are normally distributed.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract core-averaged background-subtracted DCN (3-2) spectra and fit hyperfine structure

method.value: Extract average DCN (3-2) spectrum for each of the 595 continuum cores from an elliptical aperture of 2x the continuum FWHM, subtract background spectrum from an elliptical annulus (2x to 3x continuum FWHM, excluding overlapping neighbour cores), fit single-component DCN hyperfine structure model in PySpecKit, and classify detections into Single- or Complex-type

evidence.quote: We use an elliptical aperture with a major (minor) axis length twice that of the continuum source major (minor) FWHM to extract the spectrum, where the continuum core sizes are taken from (cite: louvet22).

We extract the background emission from an elliptical annulus with an inner major (minor) axis size equal to the size of the spectral aperture (i.e. twice the continuum source major (minor) FWHM) and outer radius size 1.5x larger (i.e. three times the continuum source major (minor) FWHM).

The resulting core-average, background-subtracted spectrum for each core is then fitted using a single component hyperfine structure model (HFS) adapted for the DCN (3-2) transition in `PySpecKit` (cite: Ginsburg2011).

key_parameters.value: Core aperture = 2x continuum FWHM; background annulus = 2x to 3x continuum FWHM; detection criteria: S/N > 4 sigma (from MAD in 30 line-free channels) and velocity dispersion > 0.2 km s^-1; 7 hyperfine components from CDMS

evidence.quote: A core is determined to have a DCN (3-2) detection if a velocity dispersion of $>$0.2 km s$^{-1}$ and a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) $>$4$\sigma$ are found in the core averaged, background-subtracted spectrum.

The noise in the spectrum is estimated from the MAD in 30 continuous channels ($\sim$10 km s$^{-1}$) from either the lower or upper part of the spectrum that were identified by eye to be in a line free part of the spectrum.

assumptions.value: DCN (3-2) is an optically thin dense gas tracer with critical density ~10^7 cm^-3; FWHM linewidth = sigma_obs * sqrt(8 ln 2)

evidence.quote: We utilise the molecular transition DCN (3-2) as a proxy for the gas associated with the core as it is typically an optically thin tracer with a critical density of $\sim$10$^7$ cm$^{-3}$.

The linewidths are taken as $\sigma_{obs}\times\sqrt{8ln2}$, where $\sigma_{obs}$ is the observed velocity dispersion from single component HFS fits to the core-averaged, background-subtracted spectra.

fitting.value: Single-component hyperfine structure (HFS) model fit in PySpecKit; single-component Gaussian fit in PySpecKit for comparison lines (DCO+, OC33S, C18O, OCS, 13CS, N2D+) in G338.93

evidence.quote: The resulting core-average, background-subtracted spectrum for each core is then fitted using a single component hyperfine structure model (HFS) adapted for the DCN (3-2) transition in `PySpecKit` (cite: Ginsburg2011).
They are fitted and classified as Single- or Complex-type spectra in the same way as for DCN (3-2) (described in 4.3), but using only a single component Gaussian fit in pyspeckit.

validation.value: Visual inspection of all fitted spectra to separate Single- and Complex-type spectra; repeated extraction and fitting without background subtraction to test for background-subtraction bias

evidence.quote: This is done manually by visually inspecting all fitted DCN (3-2) spectra.
To assess if the background subtraction could bias the results, we also perform an extraction on the non-background subtracted DCN (3-2) spectra towards each core in 11.

analysis_steps.goal: Analyze core-to-core velocity dispersion, spatial spread, and non-thermal velocity dispersion across evolutionary stages

method.value: Compute core velocity offsets, core-to-core velocity dispersions, radial spatial offsets, and non-thermal velocity dispersions for the 266 Single-type cores; apply Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests between evolutionary stages and compute Pearson's correlation coefficient between non-thermal velocity dispersion and deconvolved core size

evidence.quote: In 14, we plot the core-to-core velocity dispersion vs the spatial spread (following, e.g. (cite: Stutz2016)) for each core grouped by their host region’s evolutionary stage.

In 16, we show the non-thermal velocity dispersion-size relation for the 266 cores in our sample from all 15 protoclusters, where the non-thermal velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{NT}$) is estimated assuming: $$\begin{equation} \label{eq:thermaldisp} \sigma_{NT} = \sqrt{\sigma^2 - \frac{kT_{k}}{\mu m_H}}, \nonumber \end{equation}$$

We fit Pearson’s correlation coefficient ($\rho$), which measures the linear correlation between two variables, and find a value of 0.18, indicating no correlation exists between the dispersion and core sizes in these data.

findings_qualitative.value: Global DCN (3-2) emission traces more widespread, elongated filamentary structures in evolved protoclusters compared to compact hub-type clumps in young protoclusters.

evidence.quote: In addition, we provide an overview of the DCN (3-2) emission across the ALMA-IMF protoclusters, where the global DCN (3-2) emission displays a diversity of morphology and kinematics across the sample, tracing more widespread, filamentary structures in the evolved regions, compared to young protoclusters where the DCN emission is found in more compact hub-type structures.

findings_qualitative.value: DCN (3-2) recovers the highest percentage of continuum cores with Single-type spectra in G338.93 (43%) compared to other dense gas tracers (5-31%), making it the best single proxy for core dense gas in the ALMA-IMF bandwidth.

evidence.quote: DCN (3-2) exhibits Single-type spectra towards the highest percentile ($\sim$43%) of continuum cores in G338.93, versus 5-31% for the other species.
Thus, using only a single tracer, DCN (3-2) likely still provides the best proxy of the dense gas associated with the continuum cores in the ALMA-IMF bandwidth coverage.

findings_qualitative.value: Evolved protoclusters have a significantly higher fraction of DCN-detected cores and a wider spatial distribution of cores than young and intermediate protoclusters.

evidence.quote: The evolved protoclusters have a higher percentage of DCN-detected cores, suggesting that the DCN (3-2) transition is likely a more complete tracer of the core population in evolved protoclusters.
Furthermore, the cores with DCN (3-2) detections in evolved regions tend to be more spatially extended over the region than in the younger protoclusters.

findings_qualitative.value: There is no significant difference in core-to-core velocity dispersion across evolutionary stages and no correlation between non-thermal velocity dispersion and core size.

evidence.quote: We find no obvious difference between the average core-to-core velocities and only a tentative difference in linewidths with the protocluster evolutionary stage.

We fit Pearson’s correlation coefficient ($\rho$), which measures the linear correlation between two variables, and find a value of 0.18, indicating no correlation exists between the dispersion and core sizes in these data.

claims.hypothesis: DCN (3-2) is the optimal single molecular tracer for probing the kinematics of the continuum core population within the ALMA-IMF spectral setup.
claims.experiment: Extract and fit background-subtracted core spectra for DCN (3-2), DCO+ (3-2), OC33S (18-17), C18O (2-1), OCS (19-18), 13CS (5-4), and N2D+ (3-2) towards the 42 continuum cores in G338.93.
claims.result: DCN (3-2) yields Single-type spectra towards 43% of the continuum cores across the majority of the mass distribution, compared to 5-31% for the other molecular species.
claims.finding: DCN (3-2) provides the best single-tracer proxy of dense gas associated with continuum cores in the ALMA-IMF bandwidth coverage, though a multi-line analysis is needed to recover the full core population.

evidence.quote: DCN (3-2) exhibits Single-type spectra towards the highest percentile ($\sim$43%) of continuum cores in G338.93, versus 5-31% for the other species.
Thus, using only a single tracer, DCN (3-2) likely still provides the best proxy of the dense gas associated with the continuum cores in the ALMA-IMF bandwidth coverage.

claims.hypothesis: The detection rate and spatial distribution of DCN (3-2) emission and cores evolve with the evolutionary stage of the host protocluster.
claims.experiment: Create moment maps of DCN (3-2) across all 15 protoclusters, fit HFS models to the 595 continuum cores, and compare detection rates and radial spatial offsets across Young, Intermediate, and Evolved protoclusters using KS tests.
claims.result: Evolved protoclusters have an average Single-type DCN core detection rate of 62% (75% including Complex) compared to 35% and 30% in Young and Intermediate regions, and a spatial spread standard deviation of 0.60 pc compared to 0.33 pc and 0.39 pc (significant in KS tests).
claims.finding: DCN (3-2) is more widespread and detects a higher fraction of cores in evolved protoclusters, likely due to time evolution of gas density and warmer temperatures over a larger fraction of evolved clouds.

evidence.quote: We find that DCN (3-2) is detected more often in cores situated in evolved regions with an average detection rate of 62% for cores with Single-type spectra, compared to a lower average detection rate ($<$35%) in the young and intermediate regions.
The standard deviation of the spatial spread for the young, intermediate, and evolved regions are 0.33 pc, 0.39 pc, and 0.60 pc, respectively, with standard errors $<$0.06 pc.
A KS test on the core offsets in the young and intermediate regions suggests they are drawn from a different population than cores in evolved regions.

claims.hypothesis: Core-to-core velocity dispersions and internal core linewidths vary with protocluster evolutionary stage and follow a size-linewidth relation.
claims.experiment: Compare core-to-core velocity dispersions and DCN (3-2) linewidths across Young, Intermediate, and Evolved regions using KS tests, and compute Pearson's correlation coefficient between non-thermal velocity dispersion and deconvolved core size for the 266 Single-type cores.
claims.result: Core-to-core velocity dispersions are 1.8+/-0.2, 2.6+/-0.4, and 2.2+/-0.2 km s^-1 (KS p-value not < 0.05); average linewidths are ~1.2 km s^-1 in evolved vs ~1.5 km s^-1 in young+intermediate (KS p < 0.001); Pearson's rho = 0.18 for the size-dispersion relation.
claims.finding: There is no significant difference in core-to-core velocity dispersion with evolutionary stage and no correlation between non-thermal velocity dispersion and core size, while the tentative decrease in linewidth for evolved cores requires multi-line confirmation.

evidence.quote: This suggests that the young protoclusters have a slightly smaller core-to-core velocity dispersion compared with the intermediate and evolved protoclusters; however, a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test between the core-to-core velocities of the evolutionary stages does not give $P_{values}$<0.05.

Furthermore, a KS test on the DCN (3-2) linewidths of those cores situated in the evolved regions, when compared with the DCN (3-2) linewidths of cores from intermediate $+$ young regions, gives a $P_{values}$<0.001, suggesting that they are not drawn from the same population.

We fit Pearson’s correlation coefficient ($\rho$), which measures the linear correlation between two variables, and find a value of 0.18, indicating no correlation exists between the dispersion and core sizes in these data.

why_this_data.value: ALMA-IMF homogeneously surveys 15 massive Galactic protoclusters at ~2000 au resolution across ~6.7 GHz of bandwidth; DCN (3-2) was selected because it is an optically thin tracer of dense gas (~10^7 cm^-3) that coincides well with thermal dust cores and recovers the highest fraction of Single-type core spectra.

evidence.quote: ALMA-IMF was designed to observe homogeneously 15 of the most extreme and massive Galactic clouds within a distance range of 2-5.5 kpc.
We utilise the molecular transition DCN (3-2) as a proxy for the gas associated with the core as it is typically an optically thin tracer with a critical density of $\sim$10$^7$ cm$^{-3}$.

why_this_method.value: Multi-scale tclean with a 10% primary beam mask and 5 sigma threshold avoided divergence and stippling; continuum startmodel avoided uv-plane subtraction divergence; JvM correction and radio-beam common-beam convolution ensured consistent flux scales across shallowly cleaned cubes; elliptical annulus background subtraction reduced foreground/background cloud contamination.

evidence.quote: Multi-scale deconvolution with a primary beam mask produced the most stable and optimal results over the full set of spectral windows.

As discussed previously, these cubes are not deeply cleaned due to divergence and stippling issues over the full bandwidth, which can result in significant real emission remaining in the residuals. Thus, the JvM correction provides a more accurate estimation of the flux in our data.

As with the continuum cores, where the background is filtered to estimate the core properties more accurately, we chose to perform background subtraction on the DCN (3-2) emission to limit contamination from background and foreground DCN (3-2) within the dense regions of the protocluster.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Simple uv-plane continuum subtraction prior to tclean (rejected due to complexity of data, varying dynamic range, and tclean divergence)

evidence.quote: Given the large extent of the mosaic coverage, the complexity of the data, and the varying dynamic range across an individual field, we chose not to perform a simple continuum subtraction in the uv-plane before running `tclean`.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Hogbom deconvolver, internally developed auto-masking, and CASA auto multi-threshold masking (rejected because Hogbom recovered less extended emission, auto-masking failed to cover full extended emission, and auto multi-threshold had convergence problems with multi-scale)

evidence.quote: We performed several iterations of `tclean` using the Hogbom and multi-scale deconvolvers and tested methods to mask the line emission: 1) an internally developed auto-masking, 2) the CASA auto multi-threshold masking, and 3) a primary beam mask.
Furthermore, auto multi-threshold had additional convergence problems when working with multi-scale deconvolution.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Deep cleaning thresholds of <= 3 sigma or 4 sigma (rejected due to stippling artifacts and divergence across multiple spectral windows)

evidence.quote: In addition to the stippling, we found that cleaning to levels of 4$\sigma$ or deeper also resulted in divergence across multiple spectral windows, compared with setting the noise threshold to $\geq$5$\sigma$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Non-background subtracted core spectra (tested in Appendix E.2; resulted in broader average linewidths of ~2.1 km s^-1 vs ~1.6 km s^-1 due to background contamination)

evidence.loc: Comparison of the background and non-background subtracted DCN spectra
evidence.quote: The average linewidth of the fits, however, is smaller ($\sim$1.6 km s$^{-1}$) for the background-subtracted compared with ($\sim$2.1 km s$^{-1}$) for the non-background subtracted, which is due to the removal of the background contribution.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Cleaning stopped at 5 sigma (10 sigma for G351.77) because cleaning to <=4 sigma caused divergence and stippling; core detections required S/N > 4 sigma and velocity dispersion > 0.2 km s^-1, with visual inspection filtering out Complex-type spectra.

evidence.quote: In addition to the stippling, we found that cleaning to levels of 4$\sigma$ or deeper also resulted in divergence across multiple spectral windows, compared with setting the noise threshold to $\geq$5$\sigma$.

A core is determined to have a DCN (3-2) detection if a velocity dispersion of $>$0.2 km s$^{-1}$ and a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) $>$4$\sigma$ are found in the core averaged, background-subtracted spectrum.

limitations_admitted.value: DR1 includes only 12m-array data without 7m or TP short spacings, causing negative bowls and absorption features; Band 3 spw0 (N2H+) is excluded from DR1 due to extended emission artifacts.

evidence.quote: For spectral window 0 in B3, which includes the N$_2$H$^+$ line, the 12 m only data still contain artefacts due to the extended emission and missing short spacings, we thus exclude this window from this DR1 release.
We note that in a few regions (e.g. G327.29 and G351.77), the moment 0 maps display negative bowls, resulting from the missing short spacings in this 12m-array only data.

limitations_admitted.value: Divergent channels around the V_LSR of 12CO (2-1) and C18O (2-1) were masked and left uncleaned in the final cubes, and G351.77 was cleaned only to 10 sigma.

evidence.quote: In these cases, we chose to mask the channels that showed divergence and re-run the `tclean`, leaving those channels uncleaned in the final cubes (the masked channel ranges can be obtained in the `imaging_parameters.py` file).
In the end, for this source, we ran `tclean` only down to 10$\sigma$ level for all spectral windows.

limitations_admitted.value: Overestimation of the continuum startmodel at bright hot cores with line forests causes localised negative residuals, and STATCONT continuum subtraction can be imperfect towards hot cores or bright outflows.

evidence.loc: Released line cubes and post-processed image products
evidence.quote: The `STATCONT` procedure employed simultaneously over the full spectral window can satisfactorily remove the continuum for most of the bandwidth and fields, however, towards, the positions of hot core candidates or bright outflows, the continuum subtraction could be improved.

Towards several regions that contain bright hot cores, there can be a slight overestimation of the continuum startmodel at the positions of the hot cores, resulting in localised negative features in some of the residuals.

limitations_admitted.value: 91 detected cores with Complex-type DCN spectra (typically higher mass ~17 M_sun) and 238 non-detected cores (including lowest-mass cores < 1 M_sun) are excluded from the single-component kinematic analysis.

evidence.quote: While the $V_{\rm LSR}$ from Complex-type spectral fits are provided for reference, the linewidths are not given, and these cores are excluded from the following analysis.
This may, however, be biased by the fact that we do not have estimates for all of the cores.

referee_caveats_inferred: Excluding the 91 Complex-type cores (which have the highest average mass of ~17 M_sun) from the linewidth and velocity dispersion analysis introduces a strong selection bias against massive/optically thick cores.
Core-to-core velocity dispersions change by up to a factor of 2 depending on whether sub-clusters or line-of-sight cloud components (e.g. in W51-IRS2, W51-E, G338.93) are separated.
Using 12m-only data without short spacings (7m+TP) and subtracting a local annulus background can artificially narrow linewidths and create spurious absorption features.
